clue.text: Name behind hand puppet

indicators.note: behind places the name's letter after the hand's letters

parts.note: an animal's hand or foot is a paw, and a person's hand is jokingly called one

explanation.surface: A puppet with a name sewn on behind the hand that works it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Puppet' looks like a glove puppet, but here it means a person manipulated by others.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is someone used as a tool by others, like a chess piece moved at will, so a figurative puppet.

clue.text: Keep up with twelfth man after start of point-to-point

indicators.note: after places the reserve player's letters behind the first letter
the start of a word is its first letter, here of the horse-racing term

parts.note: in cricket the twelfth man is the reserve player who fields for an injured team member

explanation.surface: A cricketer's twelfth man keeps up with a point-to-point horse race.
explanation.walkthrough: A point-to-point is a British amateur cross-country horse race; the twelfth man is cricket's substitute player.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to maintain it in good condition, which is keeping it up.

clue.text: Injury caused by a couple of cats

parts.note: a cat (cat-o'-nine-tails) is a whip used for flogging
the same cat, a flogging scourge, is also a lash

explanation.surface: Someone hurt by two cats, scratched and bitten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cats' are not animals but the cat-o'-nine-tails, an old naval scourge: two words for it sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Whiplash is a neck injury from a sudden jerk, often in car crashes.

clue.text: TV drama series provided that about Father Time?

parts.note: so can mean provided that, as in 'so long as'
pop is an informal word for father
time in the sense of ages or epochs gives eras

explanation.surface: A query whether a show, given that it concerns Father Time, counts as a drama.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Father Time' looks like one figure but splits into two pieces, and A for about is a dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Soap operas are long-running serial television dramas, so named from their soap-company sponsors.

clue.text: Girl charged nothing at first

indicators.note: at first puts the letter for nothing in front of the rest

parts.note: O, the round zero, stands for nothing
a charged wire is live, carrying current

explanation.surface: A girl was charged nothing at the start, perhaps admitted free.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like a payment but is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: Olive is a female given name, so an example of a girl.

clue.text: Cried out after prod in game

indicators.note: after puts the rearranged letters behind the prod

parts.note: to prod is to poke

indicators.note: out signals the letters of the word cried put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone cried out after being prodded during a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cried out' reads as one phrase, but 'out' rearranges CRIED into RDICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Poker dice is a game played with dice marked with playing-card faces.

clue.text: Starch up? Axe ridiculous old levy

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are made absurd, jumbled into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest about a ridiculous tax on starch, demanding it be axed.
explanation.walkthrough: Purchase tax was a British sales tax replaced by VAT in 1973.
explanation.definitionFit: Purchase tax was a former UK levy charged on goods sold, hence an old levy.

clue.text: Uncontrolled anger involving a former president

indicators.note: involving means taking the letter a inside
uncontrolled letters run wild into a new order

explanation.surface: Uncontrolled anger implicated a former president.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncontrolled' rearranges ANGER to REGAN, and 'involving' puts A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth president of the United States.

clue.text: Soon achieved in property originally having shabby exterior

indicators.note: in places the property's first letter within the shabby word
exterior says the shabby word forms the outside, round that letter

parts.note: seedy means shabby and run-down

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of property

explanation.surface: A property deal soon done, though the building looks shabby outside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Having shabby exterior' sounds like a description of the house but means SEEDY goes round P.
explanation.definitionFit: Something speedy is done quickly, so accomplished in little time.

clue.text: Correct current flowing back

indicators.note: flowing back tells you to read the word for current backwards

parts.note: a tide is a current of the sea

explanation.surface: Putting right a current that flows back the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' looks like 'present', but it is a flow of water.
explanation.definitionFit: To edit a text is to correct and revise it.

clue.text: Watch and record in paper covering American parade?

parts.note: ticker is slang for a watch
to tape is to record

explanation.surface: Watching and recording something printed in a paper about a US parade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Watch' looks like a verb but is the slang noun for a timepiece.
explanation.definitionFit: American ticker-tape parades shower the procession with shredded paper strips.

clue.text: Obscure English pieces of jewellery taken to Spain

indicators.note: taken to means the letter for Spain is added on at the end

parts.note: clips are ornamental brooches or earrings
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

explanation.surface: Little-known English jewellery shipped off to Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Obscure' looks like an adjective but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To eclipse is to block out or overshadow, which is to obscure.

clue.text: Expert calling for action intended to cause anger

parts.note: a pro is a professional, an expert
a vocation is a calling to a career

explanation.surface: An expert calling for some deliberately inflammatory action.
explanation.definitionFit: Provocation is deliberate goading meant to make someone angry.

clue.text: Embarrassed about attention after hospital listened to again

indicators.note: about means the red word wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: an embarrassed person goes red

indicators.note: after puts the attention word behind the hospital letter

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs
to give an ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: Someone embarrassed about attention after a hospital stay.
explanation.definitionFit: Reheard means heard a second time, as a court case given a fresh hearing.

clue.text: Idealists seeing sign

parts.note: seeing, the faculty of sight, is vision
Aries is a sign of the zodiac

explanation.surface: Idealists who see signs everywhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Visionaries are dreamers with grand plans, idealists rather than pragmatists.

clue.text: Canal bed I treated for lock-keeper?

indicators.note: treated letters are processed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A canal bed being treated by someone who keeps the lock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lock-keeper' suggests canals, but the lock is a lock of hair; an Alice band is a hair band.
explanation.definitionFit: An Alice band is a headband holding the hair back, keeping locks in place.

clue.text: Sleeveless garment stocked by shop in a forecourt

indicators.note: stocked by suggests the answer is carried within the shop's words, as goods on its shelves

explanation.surface: A sleeveless dress on sale at a forecourt shop.
explanation.definitionFit: A pinafore is a sleeveless apron or dress worn over other clothes.

clue.text: Seconds to destroy place under surveillance

parts.note: to take out a target is to destroy it

explanation.surface: An order to destroy a watched place within seconds.
explanation.definitionFit: To stake out a place is to keep it under covert watch, as police do.

clue.text: Novel from Hardy, for example, with surprise ending

parts.note: Oliver Hardy was the stout half of Laurel and Hardy
a twist is a surprise ending to a story

explanation.surface: A Thomas Hardy novel with an unexpected ending.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hardy' looks like the novelist Thomas Hardy but is the comedian Oliver Hardy; the novel is Dickens's.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is the novel by Charles Dickens.

clue.text: Loan shark certain to be found in ancient city

indicators.note: to be found in places the certain word inside the city

parts.note: Ur was an ancient city of Mesopotamia
sure means certain

explanation.surface: A loan shark sure to turn up in some ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: A usurer lends money at extortionate interest, just as a loan shark does.

clue.text: Conservative makes progress in times of intense trouble

parts.note: to rise is to advance or make progress

explanation.surface: A Conservative politician advances during troubled times.
explanation.definitionFit: Crises are moments of acute difficulty or danger, the plural matching 'times'.

clue.text: Top expert on the crest of a wave?

indicators.note: on in an across clue puts the expert after the wave

parts.note: surf is the foam on breaking waves
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: A top surfer riding the crest of a wave.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like 'best' describing the expert but is a noun meaning the upper face.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface is the uppermost layer or outside, the top of something.

clue.text: Number with forwards displaying well-developed abs …

parts.note: six is a number
in rugby the forwards are collectively the pack

explanation.surface: A rugby number with the forwards showing off muscular stomachs.
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby union the forwards are called the pack.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-pack is a set of sharply defined abdominal muscles.

clue.text: Energy shown by head of search party

indicators.note: head of means the first letter of search

parts.note: a team is a group or party

explanation.surface: The leader of a search party showing energy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Search party' reads as one phrase but splits in two.
explanation.definitionFit: Steam is power or vigour, as in 'running out of steam'.

clue.text: … dictates changes after their game suspended

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters behind the game

parts.note: RU is rugby union

indicators.note: changes signals the letters of dictates being altered in order

explanation.surface: Following on from the rugby players, someone dictates changes to the game.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 22-across, so 'their' refers to the forwards of the pack, whose game is rugby union.
explanation.definitionFit: A rusticated student is sent down from university for a time, suspended.

clue.text: To gain access to computer, short symbol required

indicators.note: short means the phrase is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: to log on is to gain access to a computer

explanation.surface: Logging in requires a short symbol, like a password icon.
explanation.definitionFit: A logo is a brand's emblem or symbol.

clue.text: Cause of structural damage in digs angrily received by artist and one sitting

indicators.note: received by means the jumbled letters sit within the artist

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

indicators.note: angrily suggests the letters thrown about in a temper

parts.note: an MP is a sitting member of Parliament

explanation.surface: An angry artist and his sitter find damage in their lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In digs' is the anagram fodder, not part of the definition; 'angrily' rearranges it to ISINGD.
explanation.definitionFit: Rising damp is moisture climbing walls from the ground, which harms buildings.

clue.text: International try

definitions.meaning: an international cricket or rugby match

explanation.definitionFit: A test match is an international game, and testing means trying something out.
